headline: Yields Surge on Fed Hawkishness; AI Chip Supply and Geopolitics Drive Market
summary: The week was dominated by surging US Treasury yields, driven by persistent inflation concerns and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance, including a rate hike. Geopolitical tensions continued to influence markets, with ongoing US-China talks on AI and trade, alongside hopes for US-Iran diplomatic progress. The AI sector saw significant developments in chip supply chain dynamics, with Google exploring Samsung for future TPU production, while Meta faced scrutiny over product vulnerabilities.

themes.label: Fed / Rates / Macro
themes.narrative: US Treasury yields surged across the curve, with the 30-year topping 5.5% and the 2-year reaching 2024 highs, as the Federal Reserve maintained a hawkish stance and hiked rates. Persistent inflation concerns led investors to demand higher yields, impacting equity markets.

themes.label: US Semis / AI Chips
themes.narrative: AI chip supply chain dynamics shifted, with Google exploring Samsung for future TPU production (Icefish) due to tightening TSMC capacity. Nvidia's growth projections remained strong despite valuation warnings, while its backed entity Nscale filed for IPO. Google's Gemini AI model also demonstrated security vulnerabilities during testing.

themes.label: China / Tariffs / Geopolitics
themes.narrative: US-China talks commenced on AI, trade, and critical minerals, with extended trade truces in focus. Hopes for US-Iran diplomatic progress led to a dip in oil prices, while a US-Denmark security deal on Greenland also made headlines.

themes.label: Software / Internet / Platforms
themes.narrative: Meta Platforms faced legal challenges and product vulnerabilities, impacting its market valuation, even as it tested new personal AI agents. Microsoft boosted Copilot discounts, and new AI model releases were noted alongside regulatory discussions.

themes.label: AI Infrastructure / Hyperscaler Capex
themes.narrative: Oracle encountered significant data center project delays, invoking force majeure clauses due to power-related issues. This highlights potential bottlenecks in hyperscaler capex expansion.
